written_before: any implementation of the policy and any city comparison run of this unit
user_decision_verbatim_intent: Adopt a release-timing change ONLY if it improves performance.
coordinator_interpretation: adopt only if it (a) reduces the dt=10 vs dt=5 discrepancy (accuracy) AND (b) does not worsen computational cost (peak records, peak RSS, per-step cost) beyond measurement noise

measured_problem.observation: Valley full demand, entry projection h=1 s, 25,500 s: dt=10 released 1.6949% fewer persons than dt=5 (290/295-1), journey completed vehicles -15.9%, road completed vehicles -20%
mechanism_in_code: crates/metroflow-rust/src/v1_journey.rs NativeJourneyCore::prepare evaluates the cumulative departure fraction F at the tick START t; births in (t, t+dt] are staged only at the next tick, so the state at grid time T holds released = A*F(T-dt)

entering rows retire into road offers only when born + access_delay + hold <= t (tick start); offers join the road source queue at t and the source queue admits only at the tick END t+dt (v1_road.rs step_state, pending admission after transfers, entry stamp [end,end])

Offer = (tag, mass, birth_moment, Option<entry_start>, Option<entry_end>): the interval must precede the current clock (z <= t + 1e-9) and the birth moment must satisfy B <= m*t, so the existing interval fields cannot express mass that arrives inside the current tick; they are copied into the pending part and overwritten by [end,end] at admission in interval mode
measured_problem.legacy_lag_derivation: top-level road leg, uniform births, access delay atom d with x=d mod dt uniform on [0,dt): cell admission of an individual born at tau occurs at ceil_grid(mean_birth_of_batch + d) + dt; mean (admission - individual ready time) = 1.5*dt

policy.name: release_interval_v1
policy.identity: appends ':release_interval_v1' to the whole-engine identity after the existing representation suffixes (entry_projection_support_v1/mark_block_scaled_v1); legacy identity and checkpoint bytes unchanged
semantics: top-level legs (no parent) of road and internal kind: the journey release front at the end of tick [t,t+dt) is F(t+dt), so released(T) = A*F(T) at every grid time T (each individual is released at its own birth time inside the tick)

access staging is atom-aligned: for access atom (d_k, w_k) with x_k = fmod(d_k, dt), tick [t,t+dt) stages exactly the births in (t-x_k, t+dt-x_k]; their individual ready times tau+d_k lie in one tick (t+j*dt, t+dt+j*dt], j=floor(d_k/dt), so each row is due in exactly the tick containing every one of its individual ready times; one row per atom per tick as in legacy

births in (T-x_k, T] that are released but not yet staged (the 'unstaged access mass') are active access mass; their amount A*sum_k w_k*(F(T)-F(T-x_k)) is a deterministic function of the state clock, dt, profile and law and is included in every stage/physical ledger check

entering rows are retired at the tick END deadline (t+dt+1e-10, legacy tolerance) instead of the tick start; each offer carries its in-tick arrival time tau = clamp(mean_birth + delay, t, t+dt) (mean ready time of the row); the road source queue receives it inside the tick and keeps the legacy end-of-tick admission rule, so cell entry happens at the end of the tick containing the individual ready time and never before it

road residence split for in-tick arrivals: pre-entry (inherited) += m*tau - B, source wait += m*(t+dt) - m*tau; their sum m*(t+dt)-B equals the legacy increment for the same mass; pending parts carry no interval stamp (as legacy journey offers)
child legs (with parent/eligibility): legacy release (F and eligibility at tick start, access clock from the release time); only the due deadline/arrival changes to the tick end
bus boarding and freight dispatch services are unchanged (tick-start offers, legacy accounting)
never: release or stage mass before its birth
offer or admit mass before every individual ready time of the row (top-level legs); child-leg rows are released at a grid time and all individuals share that ready time
delete, cut off, rebin beyond the named policy, or reduce demand
preserved: category mass per tag and unit (persons/vehicles/cargo through the unchanged carrier ratios)
released birth first moment (contiguous FIFO release in the fraction domain; s.7 invariant unchanged)
each row's birth first moment (exact slice mean via birth_between) and in-tick arrival first moment (B + m*delay)
road FIFO by source tick and by cell entry; movement-support boundaries and entry projection untouched (admission still a point atom at the tick end)
requested = released + pending and released = completed + active (active includes unstaged access mass)
transactional rollback, checkpoint format (only identity suffix differs), resume exactness
policy.expected_error_order: first order in dt for both policies, but with a smaller coefficient: mean admission lag after individual readiness 0.5*dt (policy) versus 1.5*dt (legacy) for top-level legs; the released ledger at grid times becomes exact (zero discretization error) for top-level legs; the dt-gap of completion curves should shrink by the release component only, because the road's own end-of-tick admission/motion discretization is unchanged
policy.oracle: the Python JointReleaseRuntime/PacketNetwork receives the same policy (same arithmetic) so that Python/Rust parity can be tested on the small fixture

fixed.tool: tools/probe_v1_refinement.py (extended: release timing selector, 60 s sampling from 25,200 s, per-call CPU seconds and native phase metrics, road ledger/moment diagnostics); legs npz from the same tool

city_comparison.sampling: hourly calls before 21,600 s; every 300 s from 21,600 to 25,200 s; every 60 s from 25,200 s to the horizon (all multiples of 10 s)
city_comparison.secondary_condition: evaluated only if all four runs reach 26,000 s; otherwise NOT_RUN and not used
city_comparison.reuse_of_prior_runs: not reused: the native binary differs from a0077a07; legacy runs are re-executed with the new binary; their checkpoints at 25,500 s are compared with the prior run checkpoints as an extra legacy identity observation only
execution_rules: one city run at a time; before each run require MemAvailable >= 6 GiB (wait otherwise, record the wait)
never kill other processes; an environment/resource failure is rerun once and both attempts are recorded
run order: legacy_dt10, interval_dt10, legacy_dt5, interval_dt5

metrics.gap_definition: gap(X) = X(dt=10) - X(dt=5) at the same simulated time, for one release timing; improvement ratio r(X) = |gap_policy(X)| / |gap_legacy(X)|

accuracy_primary.A4_destination_completed_vehicles_L1: sum over destinations |completed_vehicles_dest(dt=10) - completed_vehicles_dest(dt=5)| from the sample_legs decomposition (gap is this L1 distance itself)

accuracy_secondary_reported_only: released vehicles, journey completed persons, road released, road occupancy (released - completed)
released intent birth first moment (persons, vehicles)
road birth moment, road source-arrival moment (birth + pre-entry), road source-admission moment (birth + pre-entry + source wait - pending*T), summed cell entry moment
class (mode x purpose) completed vehicles L1
the time series of all gaps at every 60 s sample

conservation_gate.rule: every sample of every run: journey per-unit decomposition sums equal the report ledger within 1e-9 relative; road network mass residual <= 1e-9 relative and residence residual <= 1e-8 relative (recomputed from the exposed road ledger exactly as check_state); nonnegative and monotone released/completed; requested - released - pending and released - completed - active identically zero

cost.C1_peak_records: max native peak_records over calls ending at or before the comparison time
cost.C2_peak_rss_bytes: process ru_maxrss after the call ending at the comparison time
cost.C3_cpu_s_per_tick: process CPU seconds (user+system, getrusage) spent inside advance calls up to the comparison time divided by the number of ticks
cost.reported_only: wall seconds per tick (all ticks and active window 25,200-T), native tick p50/p95, native phase seconds (journey prepare, road step, finishes), construct wall

ADOPT_iff_all: G1 legacy bit identity: probe_v1_event_store.py valley_weekday_s7 25900 1 with the final binary gives checkpoint SHA-256 ab73c40f1166c92788aef865bd4f4b644359bf985a66f49182830dccf776d7ff
G2 no new failures in the specified Rust and Python regression suites (baseline 356 passed, 5 xfailed)
G3 conservation gate passes in all four runs at every sample
G4 all four runs reach 25,500 s
(a) accuracy at 25,500 s: r(A1) <= 0.9 and r(A2) <= 0.9 and r(A3) <= 0.9 and r(A4) <= 0.9
(a') if the secondary time is evaluated: r(A1..A4) <= 1.0 at 26,000 s
(b) cost, separately for the dt=10 pair and the dt=5 pair (policy / legacy at the same step), at 25,500 s and, where both runs of the pair reach it, at 26,000 s: C1 <= 1.05, C2 <= 1.05, C3 <= 1.10
adoption_rule.otherwise: NOT_ADOPT; record the failed clauses and keep legacy as the only recommended timing

threshold_rationale.accuracy_0.9: a priori materiality: at least a 10% reduction of each primary dt-gap; accuracy metrics are deterministic, so the threshold expresses materiality, not noise
threshold_rationale.records_rss_1.05: the policy admits each tick of demand one step earlier; 300 s after the 25,200 s onset that is at most dt/300 = 3.3% more released demand at the same clock (1.25% at 26,000 s), a deterministic physical shift rather than representation growth; 5% covers this shift plus allocator variation
threshold_rationale.cpu_1.10: shared host; earlier identical-configuration h runs differed by up to 8% in advance wall (92.6-100.6 s); CPU seconds are used instead of wall to reduce contention noise

adoption_rule.meaning_of_ADOPT: recommend release_interval_v1 as an explicit opt-in flag for subsequent V03 runs; the default stays legacy in this unit; V03 BLOCKED, 19/21 and 5/21 are unchanged either way

prediction_before_runs.A2_A3: reduced but nonzero (road discretization unchanged); magnitude unknown
